sentences.text: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.
The draft schedule covers payload imaging, recorder management, housekeeping activities, and expected support from the North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna.
For high-volume acquisitions, the schedule also accounts for downlink opportunities through the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna.
The Payload Processing Facility receives planning metadata needed to prepare downstream processing expectations without treating the planning schedule as a commitment to deliver products.
The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are considered during planning only to verify that expected acquisition loads remain compatible with routine processing capacity.
Juniper confirms that planned station use is compatible with network maintenance windows before the schedule is released for command preparation.
The Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Antenna Deicing Notice to assess whether planned support can proceed without adding contingency contact margin.
The Mission Planning System flags conflicts when two activities compete for the same spacecraft resource, ground station resource, or operational staffing interval.
Constraint checking includes slew time, sun-angle limits, power balance, thermal recovery time, recorder capacity, command load size, and required separation between incompatible activities.
The Flight Dynamics Team reviews cases where orbital uncertainty or contact geometry could reduce the execution margin for a planned acquisition or downlink.
The Payload Calibration Team reviews planned calibration activities when they share resources with revenue observations or affect instrument configuration states.
After schedule convergence, the Mission Planning System exports a command preparation package to the command engineering workflow at the Mission Control Center.
The Command Validation Gateway, also called Osprey in this section, performs independent validation of command stacks before they are eligible for operational approval.
Command stack validation checks syntax, timing, parameter ranges, sequencing rules, spacecraft mode compatibility, and consistency with the approved schedule baseline.
The Command Validation Gateway rejects command stacks that contain unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired configuration references, or activities outside the planning authority window.
The Telemetry Ingest Service is consulted for the latest spacecraft state needed to confirm that the command assumptions still match actual configuration and health.
The Orbit Determination Engine provides the current orbital solution used to confirm time-tagged events, contact visibility, and any attitude-dependent observation geometry.
The Product Quality Service may add planning feedback when previous acquisitions indicate that a requested geometry or instrument mode is unlikely to meet quality objectives.
The Cybersecurity Desk reviews command preparation exceptions when unusual access, emergency procedure use, or nonstandard transfer paths are requested before uplink.
Final approval requires concurrence from the Mission Control Center and the Spacecraft Operations Team before any command stack is placed in the queue for the next authorized uplink opportunity.
